title: Boss: the partner payments ticket
summary: Payments from one partner have been failing since Monday. Parse the gateway log, lock down the callback check and find the bad rows in the partner's CSV feed.

steps.title: PAY-2291: partner payments failing
body: Since Monday 08:14, payments from the partner Northwind Traders fail now and then. The ticket has three
attachments: the API gateway log, the partner's webhook settings and their nightly CSV feed. Your job:
1. Parse a gateway log line into fields.
2. Summarise the log: parsed lines, skipped lines, 5xx count and the slowest path.
3. Replace the callback URL check. Security found that it accepts look-alike hosts.
4. List the rows in the partner feed whose date or SDK version is invalid.
Use a regex where the text is flat and fixed, and a real parser everywhere else.

steps.title: A gateway log line
prompt: Gateway lines look like this:
```text
Match a whole line with the named groups `ts`, `ip`, `method`, `path`, `status`, `ms` and `req`:
- `ts`: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` in ASCII digits (validity is checked later, by a parser).
- `ip`: four dot-separated runs of one to three digits (the shape only).
- `method`: capital letters. `path`: starts with `/`, no spaces.
- `status`: 100 to 599, so a first digit of 1 to 5 and two more digits. `ms`: digits, then the literal `ms`.
- `req`: exactly eight lower-case hex digits after `req=`.

steps.title: Summarise the gateway log
prompt: Write `(int Parsed, int Skipped, int ServerErrors, string Slowest) Summarize(string[] lines)`:
- `Parsed`: lines that match the gateway format (anchor your pattern from the previous step with `^` and `$`).
- `Skipped`: lines that do not.
- `ServerErrors`: parsed lines with a status of 500 or more.
- `Slowest`: the path of the parsed line with the largest `ms` (compare numbers, not strings), or `""` when nothing
parsed. On a tie, keep the first one.
`System.Text.RegularExpressions` is imported.
starter: (int Parsed, int Skipped, int ServerErrors, string Slowest) Summarize(string[] lines)
solution: (int Parsed, int Skipped, int ServerErrors, string Slowest) Summarize(string[] lines)
if (ms > slowestMs) { slowestMs = ms; slowest = m.Groups["path"].Value; }
template: Dojo.Eq("summary of the gateway log", (5, 1, 3, "/v2/refunds"), Summarize(dojoLog));
Dojo.Eq("a line with an upper-case request id is skipped", (0, 1, 0, ""), Summarize(new[] { "2026-11-23T08:14:07Z 203.0.113.9 POST /v2/payments 502 1834ms req=9F3C1A2B" }));

steps.title: Lock down the callback check
prompt: **Symptom.** Security's report: the webhook settings page accepted `https://partner.contoso.com.evil.io/hook` and
`https://partner.contoso.com@evil.io/hook`. The current check is the regex `^https://.*partner\.contoso\.com`.
Write `bool IsAllowedCallback(string url)` with `Uri.TryCreate` instead. Allow only:
- an absolute URL with the scheme `https` on port 443 (explicit or default),
- whose host is exactly `partner.contoso.com` or ends with `.partner.contoso.com` (a subdomain).
`Uri` lower-cases the host for you. Do not use a regex.
solution: if (!Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri)) return false;
template: Dojo.Eq("a subdomain with a query", true, IsAllowedCallback("https://eu.partner.contoso.com/hook?x=1"));
Dojo.Eq("upper case is the same host", true, IsAllowedCallback("HTTPS://Partner.Contoso.com/hook"));
Dojo.Eq("user info in front of the real host", false, IsAllowedCallback("https://partner.contoso.com@evil.io/hook"));
Dojo.Eq("a host that only ends with the name", false, IsAllowedCallback("https://evilpartner.contoso.com/hook"));
Dojo.Eq("the name in the query string", false, IsAllowedCallback("https://evil.io/?next=https://partner.contoso.com"));
Dojo.Eq("not a URL", false, IsAllowedCallback("not a url"));

forbid.message: Does not use a regex for the URL

steps.title: Find the bad rows in the partner feed
prompt: The partner's nightly CSV has the columns `id,company,signed,sdk`. Company names are quoted when they contain a
comma or a quote. Write `List<string> BadRows(string csv)`: the `id` of every data row, in file order, where
- `signed` is not a real calendar date in `yyyy-MM-dd` (use `DateOnly.TryParseExact` with
`CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`), **or**
- `sdk` is not a valid semantic version: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with no leading zeros, an optional `-pre.release` and an
optional `+build.meta` (identifiers of `[0-9A-Za-z-]`, separated by single dots).
Read the CSV with `TextFieldParser`. `System.Text.RegularExpressions`, `System.Globalization` and
`Microsoft.VisualBasic.FileIO` are imported.
solution: using var parser = new TextFieldParser(new StringReader(csv));
var dateOk = DateOnly.TryParseExact(f[2], "yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None, out _);
template: Dojo.Eq("bad dates and bad versions, in file order", new List<string> { "P-002", "P-003", "P-005", "P-006" }, BadRows(dojoCsv));
Dojo.Eq("a clean feed with a quoted comma", new List<string>(), BadRows("id,company,signed,sdk\nP-010,\"A, B\",2026-01-31,0.1.0\n"));
Dojo.Eq("a leap day and a pre-release are fine", new List<string>(), BadRows("id,company,signed,sdk\nP-011,Litware,2028-02-29,1.0.0-beta.2\n"));

require.message: Reads the CSV with a real parser
